name: Asparagus (Green Soup)
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: veal, cut into small pieces
ingredients.originalText: 3 lbs. veal, cut into small pieces

instructions.text: Cut the entire stalk of the asparagus into pieces an inch long.
When the meat has boiled one hour, add half of the vegetable to the liquor in the pot.
Boil two hours longer and strain, pressing the asparagus pulp very hard to extract all the green coloring.
Add the other half of the asparagus—the heads only, which should be kept in cold water until you are ready for them, and boil twenty minutes more.
Proceed as with the asparagus white soup, omitting the milk, thickening, and salt.
The pork will supply the latter seasoning.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut the entire stalk of the asparagus into pieces an inch long.
2. When the meat has boiled one hour, add half of the vegetable to the liquor in the pot.
3. Boil two hours longer and strain, pressing the asparagus pulp very hard to extract all the green coloring.
4. Add the other half of the asparagus—the heads only, which should be kept in cold water until you are ready for them, and boil twenty minutes more.
5. Proceed as with the asparagus white soup, omitting the milk, thickening, and salt.
6. The pork will supply the latter seasoning.
